text:
## Observations

1. A square is unavailable if it is occupied or if an existing piece can capture a piece placed there.
2. Each existing piece contributes its own square and up to eight capture destinations. A destination exists only when both coordinates are between 1 and \(N\), inclusive.
3. Several pieces can contribute the same square, so each unavailable square must be counted only once. There are at most \(9M\) candidates, and a hash set can deduplicate them in expected constant time per insertion.
4. The board has \(N^2\) squares, which can be as many as \(10^{18}\). Python integers can represent this total and the final answer exactly.

## Solution sketch

> Each existing piece contributes its own square and up to eight capture destinations. A destination exists only when both coordinates are between 1 and \(N\), inclusive.

1. Read \(N\) and \(M\), and create an empty set of coordinate pairs. For each piece, insert its occupied square. Add each of the eight specified offsets to the piece’s coordinates and insert the destination only if both coordinates are within the board. This check handles corners, edges, and boards too small for any knight move.

> Several pieces can contribute the same square, so each unavailable square must be counted only once. There are at most \(9M\) candidates, and a hash set can deduplicate them in expected constant time per insertion.

2. Use the set’s size as the number of unavailable squares. The set counts overlapping capture destinations only once, including destinations that are already occupied. Processing at most nine candidates per piece takes expected \(O(M)\) time and \(O(M)\) space.

> A square is unavailable if it is occupied or if an existing piece can capture a piece placed there.

3. Subtract the set’s size from \(N^2\). Every square left in this count is empty and safe. If the set covers the entire board, the result is zero.

> The board has \(N^2\) squares, which can be as many as \(10^{18}\). Python integers can represent this total and the final answer exactly.

4. Compute the total and the subtraction using integer arithmetic, then print the result.
